subtype: Averting gaze as avoidance or respect [Interpreting]
passage: Thursday. Today I finally asked Jatin why he never looks at me when we talk. I had been reading it as him not caring, or even hiding something. It made me a bit annoyed. I asked it quietly at the water cooler, and I said I was not angry, only curious. He looked at the floor and said, "Amandeep, when I look at faces I cannot listen properly. Looking away helps me hear you." I did not know that. I said thanks and asked if it was okay for me not to expect eye contact. He said yes and looked relieved. Now I watch how he listens: he nods and repeats what I said. I was wrong to assume.

qa.q: Where did Amandeep ask Jatin about his gaze?
qa.a: Amandeep asked at the water cooler.

qa.q: What had Amandeep first thought about Jatin's averted gaze?
qa.a: Amandeep read it as not caring or hiding something, which was annoying. Jatin's explanation showed that looking away helps him listen, so the first reading was wrong.

qa.q: What did Amandeep do that worked better than assuming?
qa.a: Amandeep asked gently, said there was no anger and accepted Jatin's answer without demanding eye contact.

qa.q: How might Jatin have felt being asked about his gaze?
qa.a: He looked relieved after the explanation, so he probably appreciated the gentle question, though he may have felt a little nervous at first.

grounding: A teenager reads a peer's averted gaze cautiously and asks gently instead of assuming dishonesty or disinterest.

subtype: Averting gaze as avoidance or respect [Interpreting]
passage:
Manoj: hey, met your family today. your uncle seemed nice
Siddharth: yeah he liked you 🙂
Manoj: but when he was talking you kept looking at the floor the whole time. is everything ok? I thought you were nervous or upset
Siddharth: haha no. at home you do not look elders in the eye when they speak. it is polite, it shows respect
Manoj: oh!! I did not know that. at mine looking away means you are hiding something or you are bored
Siddharth: it is different at my house
Manoj: ok good to know. I am glad I asked. I was worrying
Siddharth: you can just ask me. I would rather that
Manoj: deal 👍

qa.q: What did Siddharth do while the uncle was talking?
qa.a: Siddharth kept looking at the floor the whole time the uncle was talking.

qa.q: What did Manoj think Siddharth's gaze meant, and what did it really mean?
qa.a: Manoj thought it might mean nervousness or upset, since at Manoj's home looking away suggests hiding something or boredom. For Siddharth it was politeness and respect toward an elder.

qa.q: What did Manoj do that was wiser than assuming?
qa.a: Manoj asked Siddharth directly and listened, and they agreed Manoj can ask again.

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel about being asked?
qa.a: Siddharth seems glad, saying it is better if Manoj just asks, and explains without irritation.

grounding: An averted gaze can mean cultural politeness, and asking gently beats assuming dishonesty or disinterest.
